title: Hybrid commitment buffer and proactive isolation proposal
content:
Overview

This doc outlines a hybrid commitment buffer model plus proactive isolation controls intended to reduce noisy-neighbor impact during short-duration surges while preserving predictable committed throughput for paying customers. Unlike pure headroom or pure burst-credit systems, the hybrid buffer mixes reserved capacity, fractional short-term credits, and an adaptive probation lane for new or bursty tenants. This is an early concept and meant to seed design discussion with SRE, billing, and product.

Problem statement

- Committed Dedicated tenants expect predictable baseline throughput, but short microbursts from other tenants can cause tail-latency spikes and contention for KV caches.
- Current burst handling either throttles immediately (hurting UX) or overcommits transiently (hurting SLOs for other tenants).
- We need a mechanism that: 1) protects baseline SLO for committed tenants, 2) allows controlled, measurable bursting for others, 3) provides a simple accounting model for billing and troubleshooting.

Goals

- Maintain 99th-percentile latency SLO for committed lanes during typical microbursts.
- Allow short bursts (seconds-to-minutes) with graceful degradation instead of hard preemption.
- Provide transparent billing signals and accounting for burst consumption.
- Offer operations playbook for handoffs and emergency throttles.

Non-goals

- Not a wholesale replacement for long-lived reserved autoscale (monthly reserved capacity).
- Not covering cross-region routing decisions or private on-prem HSM concerns.

Key concepts introduced

- Commitment Buffer (CB): a soft buffer of compute headroom per pool expressed in Commitment Units (CUs). CUs represent a normalized capacity token (roughly a fraction of a GPU slot for N seconds). Each tenant with a reserved commitment has a share of the CB proportional to their reservation. The buffer is not hard capacity but a prioritized allowance managed by the pool allocator.

- Burst Credits (BC): short-duration credits purchased or earned that let a tenant exceed their baseline for short windows. BCs have an expiration (configurable; default 10 minutes) and a decay profile. BCs come from two buckets: marketplace credits (paid) and promotional/earned credits (free).

- Probationary Lane (PL): a temporary lower-fidelity lane for tenants that suddenly expand or are new to bursting. PL traffic is routed to soft-fidelity models (quantized variants) or lower concurrency lanes to reduce contention while preserving some throughput. Tenants move out of PL automatically based on stability signals.

- Priority Spiral: an adaptive priority scoring function used to order CB allocations when contended. It blends tenant SLA weight, recent burst history, and fairness decay to avoid starvation.

Design overview

1) Pool-level state
- Each dedicated pool tracks: committed capacity, current occupancy, unused computed CB, outstanding BC balances per tenant, and PL enrollments.
- Pool exposes an API for querying headroom, active probation candidates, and CB utilization.

2) Allocation flow (request-time)
- Step A: incoming request checks baseline quota. If within baseline, regular routing.
- Step B: if above baseline, request consults BC balance; if BC available and pool-level CB not exhausted, grant extra capacity and debit BC.
- Step C: if BC absent but pool CB remains and tenant has positive priority-spiral score, grant transient CB allowance and mark as provisional (subject to later reconciliation).
- Step D: if neither BC nor CB can be granted, attempt PL routing (lower-fidelity), then graceful throttle with retry hints.

3) Autoscaling interplay
- Autoscaler remains the canonical source for capacity adds. CB is designed to reduce noisy autoscale churn by absorbing microbursts and giving the autoscaler a window to react.
- Autoscaler triggers thresholds are adjusted by CB state: e.g., if CB consumed above X% for Y minutes, autoscaler will provision and replenish CB accordingly.

4) Accounting and billing
- Baseline committed usage billed per contract as before.
- BC usage shows up as a separate line item (consumed credits). Marketplace BCs are monetized; promotional BCs are zero-cost but visible in usage reports.
- Provisional CB consumption does not immediately bill; instead a reconciliation batch runs hourly: if provisional usage persists beyond a configurable threshold (default 15 minutes continuous), convert provisional consumption into BC charges or trigger tenant outreach.

5) Isolation controls and safety nets
- Soft-fencing: tenants below a configurable priority threshold are limited to PL once proportional fairness is violated for N consecutive minutes.
- Emergency degrade: SRE can trigger a pool-wide degrade that forces all PL-eligible traffic into PL and caps provisional CB to zero.
- Quarantine: repeated overuse moves a tenant into temporary quarantine where only baseline is allowed until manual review. Quarantine history feeds into account escalations and potential billing refunds.

Algorithms and parameters (initial proposal)

- CU definition: 1 CU ~= 0.02 of a GPU slot for 60s (tunable). Use CUs to avoid hardware-specific units in control plane.
- Default pool CB size: 5% of pooled reserved capacity converted to CUs.
- BC default expiry: 10 minutes for earned credits, 1 month for purchased marketplace credits.
- Priority Spiral: score = w1*SLA + w2*(1 - recent_burst_fraction) + w3*(fairness_decay), weights [0.5,0.3,0.2] initial.
- Provision-to-bill window: 15 minutes. If provisional consumption persists beyond this, bill against BC or notify.

Operational UX and runbook snippets

- On a microburst: CB absorbs; autoscaler sees rising occupancy but CB low -> autoscaler queues provision request. If provision takes > 5m, controller converts provisional usage to PL routing for lower-risk tenants.
- On repeated contention: operations dashboard highlights tenants with >20% provisional consumption in last hour. SRE paged for pools where PL traffic > 40% and CB exhausted.

Telemetry and observability

- Metrics to emit per pool: cb_total_cu, cb_used_cu, bc_balance_tenant_{id}, provisional_consumption_tenant_{id}, pl_enrolled_count, avg_pl_latency.
- Dashboards: per-pool headroom heatmap, tenant provisional history, billing reconciliation events.
- Tracing: tag requests with reason_code (baseline|bc|cb-provisional|pl|throttled) for downstream correlation.

Rollout plan (phases)

- Phase 0 (lab): simulation-only with historic traces to tune Priority Spiral weights and provision-to-bill windows.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable CB and PL in a single non-production pool; expose telemetry and reconcile logic but disable billing conversion.
- Phase 2 (beta): enable in a subset of committed customers (opt-in) with billing conversion for marketplace BC only. Provide UI in Console to inspect BC and provisional usage.
- Phase 3 (GA): full rollout, default CB enabled for all pools with aggressive monitoring and SLO adjustments.

Open questions / tradeoffs

- What's the right CU definition to balance cross-GPU homogeneity vs. perceptible billing granularity?
- Provision-to-bill window sensitivity: short windows deter abuse but increase billing churn and surprise; long windows increase risk to baseline SLOs.
- Complexity vs. Explainability: the hybrid model is richer but harder for customers to reason about. How much telemetry/UI do we need to make this acceptable?

Next steps

- SRE: run a 2-week simulation on representative traces (assign to Ethan).
- Billing: finalize billing treatment for provisional-to-charged conversion and invoice labeling (Sofia).
- Eng (autoscaler): prototype CB tracker and provisional ledger APIs (Carlos).
- Product: draft Console mockups for BC visibility and PL toggles (Aditi).

References and related artifacts

- Related runbooks: /shared_drives/product/dedicated/tenant-harmony-autoscale-playbook-and-iso-sabbatical-proposal.json (for reference)
- Simulation notes: JIRA-DED-4123
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-autoscaler/pull/78

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally design-forward with some new naming. Biggest asks: 1) sanity-check CU sizing heuristic, 2) validate reconciliation & billing flow, 3) feedback on PL fidelity tradeoffs. Add comments inline or reply in the Slack thread linked above.
